pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Individual dark regions exhibit soft, diffused edge gradients with smooth pixel transitions. Geometry varies from irregular, multi-pointed stellate patterns on the posterior flank to larger, more rounded amorphous configurations on the central flank.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: The light pelage forms a continuous, high-thickness network of pathways separating the patches. Junction nodes are numerous and well-defined, with the negative space occupying a significant proportion of the visible surface area.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A localized dark textural disruption is visible on the lower ventral flank, situated beneath a perched oxpecker, appearing as a focal skin lesion or site of parasitic activity.
other_distinctive_markers: Presence of two oxpeckers (Buphagus sp.) on the dorsal rump and lower ventral flank. Significant foreground occlusion by a complex network of dry, leafless woody branches.
